newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end tad higher in token session. [CORRECTED 22:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end tad higher in token session. [CORRECTED 22:35 GMT]

text.p: Argentine blue chips crawled higher Monday, recording their eleventh consecutive gain, but volume slowed down to a trickle due to the U.S. Memorial Day holiday, dealers said.
"Absolutely nothing happened today -- the week really begins tomorrow when Wall Street resumes trade," said Miguel Daneri at Boston Securities brokers.

The blue-chip MerVal index edged up 0.2 percent (corrects figure from 1.2 percent) to 768.92, while floor volume shrank to 12.6 million pesos from 22 million Friday and an average daily tally of 30 million earlier last week.
"I think the market will push cautiously higher and settle at 775-780 this week, always keeping a very selective tone," Daneri said.
The broad market closed off 0.1 percent, with winners beating losers 29 to 16 and 22 stocks closing flat.

Best blue-chip performers were electricity generator Central Puerto and oil company Astra, which rallied 3.9 percent and 3.5 percent, respectively. Traders said Astra, controlled by Spain's Repsol, rose on rumors Repsol was buying stock and increasing its stake in the company.
Steelmaker Siderca and conglomerate Comercial del Plata tacked on 1.9 percent and 1.5 percent, respectively.

The heaviest MerVal losses were for carmakers Sevel and Ciadea, which slumped 3.4 percent and 2.6 percent, respectively, foods giant Molinos, off 1.8 percent, Banco de Galicia, off 1.6 percent, and Telecom and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, both down 1.1 percent.
